S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

patient_info.stressor: When Vilma's production company underwent a major business readjustment, her previously solitary camera and editing routines were replaced by faster multi-person documentary shoots, live client reviews, and rotating assistant crews. Over the next 2 years and 2 months, what she had once managed through bullet-journals and strict private routines became clinically significant: she made avoidable technical errors, seemed not to take in direct instructions, could not stay seated through post-production meetings, and repeatedly jumped into conversations before producers finished. Her constant movement on set and intrusive corrections began delaying shoots and weakening her bid for a senior director of photography role, creating clear occupational impairment despite her technical skill. After nearly losing a heritage documentary contract because of these patterns, she used her industry health plan to seek a psychiatric evaluation on her own.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: What finally scared me into coming in is that I keep making dumb technical mistakes I know better than to make, like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third even after I’ve checked it.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: When a producer gives me a direct note on set, I’ll be looking right at them, but my brain has already jumped to the lens change or the next shot, and then I have to ask them to say it again like I wasn’t standing there.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: In edit reviews I’m constantly clicking a pen, bouncing my knee under the table, or rolling my chair back and forth, and people have started joking that they can hear me before they see me.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: If a meeting runs longer than a few minutes, I’m up getting water, checking a cable, adjusting a monitor, or finding some excuse to move instead of staying in my seat like everyone else.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Sitting still through a client screening feels like there’s pressure building under my skin, like I need to get up and do something with my body even when I know I’m supposed to just watch quietly.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: Even on lighter shoot days I move from packing gear to tweaking camera settings to reorganizing bins in the edit bay without really stopping, and my assistants tell me it’s exhausting just trying to keep up with me.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: I jump in with answers before the director or client has finished their question, and sometimes halfway through I realize I answered the wrong thing because I reacted to the first few words.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I catch myself cutting into other people’s conversations or leaning over an assistant’s shoulder to fix something on their timeline before they’ve asked for help, and it comes off like I don’t trust them.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Even in elementary school, teachers moved my desk because I was always out of my seat, blurting answers, or bothering classmates before I realized I was doing it.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My producers have started trusting me less on complex shoots, and my chance at moving into a senior director of photography role has been slipping despite the quality of my camera work.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: It has been going on at this disruptive level for about two years and two months, since the company readjustment changed how my shoots and edit reviews run.
